A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same proxy-explanation research, and all supplied pages are readable. However, v1 refers to an appendix and supplemental documentation that are absent from the supplied PDF, limiting comparison with v2's Appendices A-I.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-model fidelity experiments on SST, MMLU and Natural Questions (Figures 2-4), plus a repeated prompt-compression experiment (Table 2).

after.justification: v2 reports original fidelity, screening, cost, compression and poisoned-example-removal results, together with sensitivity analyses and detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: v2 introduces offline task-level screening using sequential paired tests, followed by online agreement checking and an oracle fallback policy (Section 3, Algorithm 1). Prediction-agreement filtering already appeared in v1; the substantial addition is the explicit statistical selection procedure replacing v1's acknowledged heuristic proxy selection.

E1.justification: The original SST/MMLU/Natural Questions coverage is retained. v2 adds fidelity evaluations on Large Movie Review, Fake News and Web Question, extends compression to HellaSwag, GSM8K and PIQA, and reports poisoned-example removal on SST, HellaSwag and PIQA (Figure 4, Tables 4-5).

E2.justification: v1's compression comparison uses random deletion and oracle guidance as the normalization reference. v2 Table 4 retains these comparisons and adds evaluated AttnComp and LLMLingua baselines, substantially strengthening the comparator set beyond random deletion.

E3.justification: v2 introduces screening evaluation with a 0.9 fidelity threshold, maximum sample size 50, and precision/recall/F1 metrics. Compression changes its target from DeepSeek V3 to GPT-4o and replaces oracle-normalized MDTA with the fraction of original examples removed. Natural Questions changes from reported AOPC to accuracy, although v2 retains the regression formulation without explaining that accuracy calculation.

E4.justification: v2 adds screening-reliability evaluation, sensitivity of screening precision and recall to maximum sample size (Table 3, Appendix F), and a poisoned-example-removal case study. Agreement filtering was already analyzed in v1 and is retained in expanded displays. v1's separate Natural Questions attribution-deletion/AOPC analysis is absent from v2.

E5.justification: v1 reports 15 compression repetitions and averages, without confidence intervals in the supplied PDF. v2 retains 15 repetitions, specifies varying examples and test questions, adds 95% confidence intervals for SST/MMLU fidelity, and introduces sequential screening with 99% t-intervals. This establishes expanded statistical reporting, not an increase in the compression run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds cost, screening, additional-benchmark and poisoning results (Tables 2-5, Figure 4). For example, SST accuracy after poisoning removal is 94.0% with proxy explanations, 94.2% with oracle explanations and 87.1% with random deletion. Retained values also change: DeepSeek V3's SST Kernel SHAP oracle accuracy is 0.58 in v1 Figure 2 versus 51.67% in v2 Table 7. Compression results use changed settings and cannot establish a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal definitions for agreement-conditioned screening, paired fidelity differences and screening decisions, alongside new cost decomposition and revised compression definitions. These are operational mathematical additions; neither version supplies a transferability theorem or a proof of the screening guarantee.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims empirical feasibility of inexpensive proxy explanations with comparable fidelity. v2 makes statistically screened reliability and actionable optimization central contributions, claims over 90% fidelity with an 88.2% cost reduction, and explicitly adds poisoned-example-removal utility. The benchmark-release contribution is retained and named XLLM-Bench.

C2.justification: v2 interprets screening precision and near-threshold false positives as evidence of reliability, and adds a subject-dependent explanation of fidelity in Appendix G. Its limitations replace v1's heuristic-selection concern with possible misalignment on difficult reasoning tasks, reduced savings from fallback, and prospective proxy fine-tuning. v1's explanation of DeepSeek Kernel SHAP instability is no longer discussed.

D1.justification: v1 supplies basic perturbation and deployment settings while referring readers to unavailable supplemental documentation. v2 provides a code/data access link and appendices documenting implementations, query caching, prompt templates, probability extraction, decoding settings, hardware and unquantized deployment. It also reports approximately 3,000 GPU-hours and $20,000 in API expenditure. These are substantial additions to the supplied reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around LLM homogeneity and explanation-guided prompt optimization, citing works including Jiang et al. (2025), Lee et al. (2025), Shin et al. (2020) and Tenney et al. (2024). It removes v1's discussion of generated self-explanations and their faithfulness literature, while retaining the relationship to complementary explanation-acceleration methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around actionable interpretability. Background and related work are merged, a dedicated framework section is introduced, fidelity evaluation is reorganized around three research questions, and the case-study narrative becomes a two-task utility evaluation. v2 also adds an author and substantial appendix structure.

P2.justification: v2 changes from single-column to two-column presentation, edits and relocates the workflow diagram, and adds a motivation diagram, screening plots and multiple comparison tables. Main-text heatmaps become compact selected-model panels, with extensive appendix heatmaps and confidence-interval tables. Some new labels are inconsistent: Figure 7's caption describes LIME, but its right panel is labeled Kernel SHAP.

improvement.justification: v2 improves assessability and reproducibility through explicit proxy selection, screening/fallback cost accounting, substantive compression baselines and detailed implementation and uncertainty reporting. However, it replaces v1's defined Natural Questions AOPC evaluation with unexplained accuracy, introduces inconsistent appendix labels, and claims screening confidence without justifying repeated use of fixed-level intervals. These weaknesses limit the net benefit despite the substantial expansion.
